after-multiline.summary: a statement that spans several lines is followed by a blank line
after-multiline.message: add a blank line after the multi-line statement above

switch-clauses.summary: a blank line goes in between switch clauses and none is ever removed; the gap under a fall through label with an empty body is left as it is
switch-clauses.message: add a blank line between these switch clauses

edge-blank.summary: a block has no blank line right after `{` or right before `}`

guard-join.summary: a single-line declaration or assignment is followed directly by an `if` that references what it binds, whatever the body size and with or without `else`
guard-join.message: remove the blank line between `{name}` and the `{reader}` that reads it

consume-join.summary: a single-line declaration or assignment is followed directly by a `return` or `switch` that references what it binds
consume-join.message: remove the blank line between `{name}` and the `{reader}` that reads it

use-join.summary: a single-line declaration is followed directly by a loop, `try` or function declaration that references what it binds
use-join.message: remove the blank line between `{name}` and the `{reader}` that reads it

guard-chain.summary: consecutive compact guards (`if` with a single statement body and no `else`) have no blank line between them
guard-chain.message: remove the blank line between these compact guards

let-step.summary: a `let` that joins the block below it gets a blank line above it, so it starts its own step
let-step.message: add a blank line above this `let`, the block below assigns or uses it

after-guard.summary: a single-line guard that returns, throws, continues or breaks is followed by a blank line, unless the next statement is an `if` or a jump (`return`, `throw`, `break`, `continue`)
after-guard.message: add a blank line after the guard above, a new step starts here

short-body.summary: a block of 2 or 3 compact statements has no blank lines, whether it is a function body, an arrow body, a method, a nested block or a switch clause body
short-body.message: remove the blank lines between these 2 or 3 compact statements

braces.summary: a control flow body that is a single statement has no braces
braces.message: remove the braces around this single statement body

block-spacing.summary: a multi-line block directly under a statement, when no join rule explains it
block-spacing.message: add a blank line above this block, or join it to the step above

wall.summary: 6 or more consecutive single-line statements with no blank line, reported only where a blank line `--fix` keeps can split the run
wall.message: split these {n} statements into steps with a blank line

flags: apply every deterministic rule in place
files from `git diff --name-only HEAD` plus untracked files
with --changed or --staged, only gaps and blocks touching changed lines
the staged content of staged files, for pre-commit
source on stdin; --fix: fixed text on stdout, findings on stderr; --check: findings on stdout
turn on the braces rule even when lint config turns it off or cannot be read
turn off the braces rule, keep the blank line rules
which rule decides the gap or braced body at that line, and why
Stop and SubagentStop; PostToolUse on Edit, MultiEdit and Codex `apply_patch`; PreToolUse on Write; reads JSON on stdin
usage, flags and the rule catalog
the version, and for a built binary the commit it was built from
usage:
Usage: stanza (--fix | --check) [--changed [--hunks] | --stdin <path> | [--] <paths...>] [--json] [--braces | --no-braces]
       stanza --check --staged [--hunks] [--json] [--braces | --no-braces]
       stanza explain [--no-braces] [--] <file>:<line>
       stanza hook [--braces | --no-braces] [--hunks]
